compactMembership.notes: Texas's electrician reciprocity operates via named bilateral agreements with individual states, not a single multistate compact license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact). Recorded as false to avoid conflating these bilateral agreements with a compact under this field's actual schema meaning.

reciprocityRules.value: Texas has confirmed Journeyman Electrician reciprocity agreements with: Alaska, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Montana, Nebraska, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Wyoming, and Alabama. North Carolina and Louisiana have Master-only agreements with Texas — their Journeyman reciprocity status is not confirmed by any official TDLR source found. Ohio's official March/June 2026 TDLR announcement explicitly confirms Master-level reciprocity but does not mention Journeyman — Ohio Journeyman reciprocity is UNKNOWN, neither confirmed nor denied by any official source found.

reciprocityRules.notes: Alaska/Arkansas/Idaho/Iowa/Montana/Nebraska/NewMexico/Oklahoma/SouthDakota/Wyoming confirmed directly by TDLR's primary out-of-state.htm page. Alabama confirmed by the official 2026-03-20 TDLR announcement (explicitly names both journeyman and master). Ohio-Journeyman deliberately left as an open, explicit Unknown per Phase 2F.1's finding — the official Ohio announcement only names 'master electricians and master electrical contractors,' never mentioning journeyman either way.

endorsementRules.notes: TDLR's official materials use the term 'reciprocity' specifically for these named agreements; a separately-named general 'endorsement' pathway distinct from reciprocity was not confirmed in Phase 2F/2F.1 research.

requiredExams.value: Applicants must have taken and passed the reciprocal state's own statewide examination for electrical work — Texas does not require a separate Texas exam under reciprocity, but TDLR verifies the original exam was passed via a letter of good standing from the issuing state.
